result:
Parking the roadmap. Stage 2 (closure notices) and the three Ranked-list items each go to `specs/deferred_items.md` as one deferred item. Then the roadmap moves to `specs/completed/`, marked `PARKED (2026-11-06) — 1 of 2 stages complete`. The Ranked-list items are not committed stages, so they don't count in the "of 2".

**1. Read the item schema and check the target files exist**

```
Read ~/.claude/skills/writing-plans/references/deferred-backlog.md   # the Deferred-item schema
Read specs/deferred_items.md                                          # may not exist yet
Bash: ls specs/completed/
```

**2. Append to `specs/deferred_items.md`** (creating it if missing). This is the draft. I'll match its fields to the schema from step 1 before writing.

```markdown
## lock-closures-roadmap — 2026-11-06

Parked from specs/completed/lock-closures-roadmap.md when the canal study's funding ended. Stage 1's result and cost are in specs/lock-closures-stage-1-findings.md.

- [ ] Closure notices by email (was Stage 2, Track B, O5)
      Boat operators get an email notice within an hour of a lock closing, from the closure log's live feed, sent to an operator mailing list.
      Size: small. One closure-log poll every 10 minutes. The live feed's existence is unverified.
      Done when: in a test, an email reaches every address on the mailing list within an hour of a new closure entry.

- [ ] 7-day closure-risk outlook per lock (was Ranked list A #1, O2)
      Turn the river-level forecast into a 7-day closure-risk outlook for each lock, using Stage 1's gauge-level response curve (steep above 3.1 m).
      Size: small. One model run a day. Stage 1's fit took 22 minutes on a laptop.
      Done when: a 7-day outlook for each lock exists from a real river-level forecast, with its run time recorded.

- [ ] Per-lock closure curves, pooled (was Ranked list A #2, O3)
      Separate closure-vs-gauge-level curves for all 14 locks, pooled across locks.
      Size: medium. About 14 times Stage 1's 1.8 GB of data. Stage 1 found the four longest-record locks show close to the same curve.
      Done when: pooled curves for all 14 locks are fit on real data, with result and measured cost written down.

- [ ] Closure-history map for boat operators (was Ranked list A #3, O4)
      A static map page showing each lock's closure history, for the canal's boat operators.
      Size: about a day of work.
      Done when: the map page shows closure history for all 14 locks from the real closure log.
```

Stage 2 left out text-message notices, and no stage or list item picks them up. So they get no item.

**3. Mark and move the roadmap**

Add this under the title of `specs/lock-closures-roadmap.md`:
```markdown
> PARKED (2026-11-06) — 1 of 2 stages complete. Remaining stage and Track A's Ranked list moved to specs/deferred_items.md, section "lock-closures-roadmap — 2026-11-06". Reason: the canal study's funding ended.
```
```
Bash: git mv specs/lock-closures-roadmap.md specs/completed/lock-closures-roadmap.md
```

There is no spec, methodology file or critique file behind this roadmap, so nothing else retires with it. `specs/lock-closures-stage-1-findings.md` stays where it is, because the deferred items point to it.

**4. Commit on `main`**

```
Bash: git add specs/deferred_items.md specs/completed/lock-closures-roadmap.md && git commit -m "Park lock-closures roadmap (1 of 2 stages complete): funding ended; remaining work to deferred_items"
```

After the commit, the roadmap is out of `specs/` and nothing routes from it. If funding returns, all four items are in the deferred backlog, and `/deferred` can promote them.
